subject: Reconciling notification window, subprocessor handoff, and jurisdictional data flow
messages:
From: Dana Morris <security@finedge.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Aaron Blake <aaron.blake@finedge.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Clarify notification window + subprocessor evidence path

Karthik —

Thanks again for taking time on short notice. We ran through your DPA draft with Legal and Security. Two operational clarity items that are blockers for our InfoSec board sign-off:

1) Notification window: your current DPA states "as soon as reasonably practicable" and then a 72‑hour target for confirmed customer-impacting incidents. We need an explicit maximum timeline (we proposed 72 hours for confirmed incidents, 120 hours for incidents under investigation) and a clear escalation path if evidence needs to cross borders.

2) Subprocessor evidence handoff: as a cloud vendor with subprocessors in the US, we need to know who is the designated liaison for evidence transfer (forensics images, system logs) and whether Redwood will accept secure transfer to our EU‑hosted escrow or require Redwood to push data to a gateway. Which teams own this?

Can you confirm: a) single point of contact for evidence handoff, b) max time to furnish preservation evidence once the incident is confirmed, c) whether Redwood accepts customer‑initiated private transfer to our EU SFTP?

Attachments: sample evidence matrix (placeholder) — we will use it to map data types and locations.

Appreciate a tight turnaround — our board meets Wednesday.

—Dana
Security Lead, FinEdge Systems

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Morris <security@finedge.com>
Cc: Aaron Blake <aaron.blake@finedge.com>, monica.patel@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify notification window + subprocessor evidence path

Dana —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level responses up front, followed by a short proposed checklist we can commit to in the DPA redline. Monica, Ben — can you review the procedural bullets and confirm operational feasibility?

High level answers:
- Single liaison: Redwood Security (sec-incident@redwood.ai) will be the primary contact; we will also supply a named on-call for each incident (Role: Incident Liaison) within 2 hours of confirmation.
- Maximum timelines: Redwood can accept a contractual maximum of 72 hours for confirmed customer-impacting incidents (to provide initial notification + preliminary assessment). For incidents requiring deeper preservation evidence (forensic images, encrypted KV logs), we propose a maximum of 5 business days to produce preserved artifacts, unless legal/regulatory holds prevent transfer.
- Cross-border transfer: Redwood supports secure push to an EU SFTP or transfer to a customer‑managed escrow, provided legal review and export controls permit. We will not unilaterally transfer data outside the EU for EU‑resident customer data without documented authorization.

Proposed DPA checklist items (for inclusion as an appendix):
1) Definitions: "Confirmed customer‑impacting incident" vs "Potential incident under investigation" with examples.
2) Notification timing: Initial notification (72 hours for confirmed incidents); status updates at 24‑48 hour cadence until containment.
3) Evidence preservation: Redwood to preserve volatile artifacts immediately; produce preserved artifacts within 5 business days unless blocked by law enforcement order or export control.
4) Liaison and transfer options: Primary contact sec-incident@redwood.ai; support for customer EU SFTP or third‑party escrow; transfer method and transfer logs recorded in the incident record.
5) Subprocessor coordination: Redwood will route subprocessor evidence requests through our contractually obligated subprocessors; timelines depend on subprocessor location and applicable controls — we propose explicit SLA buckets (EU subprocessors: 5 business days; non‑EU subprocessors: variable + notice).

If that sounds aligned I'll have Legal prepare a redline that incorporates the explicit timelines and a short escalation ladder (Customer SOC -> Redwood Security -> Redwood General Counsel).

-Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Dana Morris <security@finedge.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify notification window + subprocessor evidence path

Looping in Legal/Trust ops to confirm the 5 business day preservation SLA and subprocessor buckets. A few operational clarifications from CS side:

- We need to confirm whether "preserved artifacts" includes full VM snapshots, or a curated export (logs + KV cache exports + auth traces). For most customers we provide curated exports first to get investigators started and full forensic images on request.
- If customer elects EU SFTP, we need their support contact + acceptance of a transfer manifest format.
- For EU‑resident PII, Redwood will not initiate outbound transfer outside EU without documented authorization (to match your ask). However, we need to add a clause about lawful requests (subpoena/Law Enforcement) and notification reciprocity.

Ben/Laura please confirm the feasibility and any capacity implications — full VM snapshots can be heavy and sometimes require dedicated engineering time.

-Monica
Head of Customer Success (Redwood Inference)

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Dana Morris <security@finedge.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify notification window + subprocessor evidence path

Monica/Karthik —

Operational confirm: curated export (logs + KV cache snapshot + auth traces) achievable within 5 business days for EU‑hosted customers on standard Dedicated/Private plans. Full VM snapshots require engineering provisioning; estimate 10 business days and will be treated as an elevated ops activity (we can include as an optional line item in the DPA appendix).

We can support secure push to customer EU SFTP. Need: SFTP host, username, fingerprint, and an acceptance email acknowledging responsibility for stored artifacts.

If FinEdge requires that Redwood initiate transfer into their escrow, that is acceptable so long as FinEdge signs the escrow acceptance and we have a chain‑of‑custody manifest signed by both parties.

-Ben
Senior Ops, Redwood Dedicated Services

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Morris <security@finedge.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify notification window + subprocessor evidence path

Dana —

Thanks — based on internal review here's a concise set of commitments we can add to the DPA redline tomorrow:

A) Notification: initial confirmed incident notification within 72 hours; status updates every 48 hours until containment or formal handoff.
B) Preservation & delivery: curated artifacts delivered within 5 business days; full forensic images quoted at 10 business days (optional).
C) Liaison & transfer: sec-incident@redwood.ai + named on‑call within 2 hours; support for customer EU SFTP or customer‑managed escrow with signed transfer manifest.
D) Subprocessors: Redwood to route evidence requests to subprocessors; subprocessor response SLAs: EU subprocessors (5 business days), non‑EU subprocessors (subject to local restrictions; Redwood will notify customer and escalate).
E) Exceptions: law enforcement orders, export controls, or export licensing will supersede timelines; Redwood will notify customer if such an exception applies and provide rationale.

I'll attach an initial redline and a condensed checklist for your board meeting. If FinEdge agrees to the redline language we'll add the appendix to the DPA and push for a signoff by end of week.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: evidence_manifest_stub.pdf; redlines_dpa.docx
